title: NYC’s AI Office Boom Is Bust for Young Job Hunters, Report Finds
key_facts: A Partnership for New York City report, covered by Bloomberg, says AI companies leased more than 2.2 million square feet of New York office space in the first half of 2026, more than twice their total for all of 2025.
New York AI startups raised a record $16.7 billion in venture capital last year, second only to the San Francisco Bay Area.
New York added just 38,000 private-sector jobs in 2025, roughly half the previous year's increase, and employers leaned toward experienced workers.
Since ChatGPT's release in 2022, entry-level postings fell 41% in design, media and writing, 31% in administrative work, 27% in business management and 23% in finance.
Entry-level postings that ask for AI skills rose 55% over the same period.
The report does not establish that AI alone caused the hiring slowdown; economists also point to remote work, which can make training junior staff harder.
Partnership chief executive Steve Fulop warned that office leases are not proof of hiring: AI firms sign shorter leases and some have yet to build large local workforces.
The New York City Council is due to hear from major AI companies next week on possible safeguards.
quote_evidence: AI companies leased more than 2.2 million square feet of office space across the city in the first half of 2026—more than twice their total for all of 2025.
The report does not establish that AI alone caused the hiring slowdown.
Fulop also cautioned against treating office leases as evidence of immediate hiring.
why_it_matters_hint: AI companies are filling New York offices, but the report finds fewer entry-level openings in fields exposed to AI, which could shut young workers out of first jobs; cause is not proven.
event_date: Report published around 2 Oct 2026 (covers first half of 2026 and 2025 data)
